expectations.text: Explains the obligation mechanism: the ISM applies to the provider contractually — the provider implements ISM controls appropriate to the classification of the data handled, and the customer agency remains the authorising party
expectations.evidence: 'the agency's obligations under the ISM and PSPF flow down to you contractually... The agency remains accountable for the security of the system and the information it holds/processes... your obligation exists because the contract requires it.'

expectations.text: Answers the IRAP question correctly: yes in practice — commercial cloud providers serving government undergo IRAP assessments (whose reports agencies consume for their authorisation decisions); private-sector status does not exempt the provider
expectations.evidence: 'Being privately owned does not exempt you — the requirement attaches to the data/system being handled, not to your organisational status... you'll need to engage an ACSC-endorsed IRAP assessor, prepare the same artefacts a government system would... and go through the assessment process.'

expectations.text: Identifies the critical cloud control areas: tenant isolation, ASD-approved cryptography for data in transit (noting the June 2026 expansion to all data-in-transit scenarios) and at rest, access control with MFA, event logging/monitoring accessible to the agency, and personnel security
expectations.evidence: Explicitly covers 'Data encryption at rest and in transit, using ASD Approved Cryptographic Algorithms and Protocols', 'strong authentication (MFA)', 'Tenant isolation and multi-tenancy controls', 'comprehensive audit logging... notification obligations to the agency', and 'Personnel security — background checks/security clearances'. Does not mention the June 2026 in-transit crypto expansion specifically, but covers all other required elements.

expectations.text: Requires a documented shared-responsibility matrix (which ISM controls the provider vs the agency owns) and contractual security terms (incident notification to the agency, evidence/assurance provision, right to audit)
expectations.evidence: 'often documented in a Shared Responsibility Matrix', 'Audit and assessment rights — whether the agency or its delegate... can assess your environment', 'Incident notification obligations and timeframes', and 'evidence provision requirements' are all explicitly named.

expectations.text: Addresses data sovereignty/residency and supply-chain transparency (subcontractors, support locations) as agency-facing obligations
expectations.evidence: 'Data sovereignty/data residency requirements (data must often stay within Australia...)', 'Subcontractor/fourth-party flow-down requirements', and 'no offshore admin access without agency sign-off' explicitly address sovereignty, subcontractors, and support-location obligations.
